newsitem.title: USA: Dow posts biggest loss in month in nervous trading.
newsitem.headline: Dow posts biggest loss in month in nervous trading.

text.p: U.S. blue chips skidded to their biggest point loss in one month as earnings jitters heightened and traders used a market rumor, later denied, that Russian President Boris Yeltsin had died as an excuse to take profits.

The Yeltsin rumor "was just one excuse. The real essence of the decline was the fear of earnings and, from a technical standpoint, the market's failure over the past two days to close above 6000," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments.
The Dow industrials lost 36 to about 5930.
It was the biggest loss since September 5's 49.94 point drop and followed Monday and Tuesday's total 26 point drop.

After topping 6000 for the first time ever on Monday intraday and breaching the major milestone briefly on Tuesday, the Dow did not even flirt with that level on Wednesday. Birinyi Associates Inc tracked five sell programs in the morning and early afternoon that wiped 65 points off the Dow.
The S&P 500 lost four to about 697.
But the tech-laden Nasdaq Composite ended only modestly lower, off two to about 1238 as most chip stocks maintained strong gains after a bullish September book-to-bill report.

Bellwether Intel lost 3/4 to 100-7/8 but strong chip and chip-related issues included Texas Instruments, up two to 57-1/8, Micron, up 7/8 to 32-3/8, Atmel, up 1-5/8 to 34-1/8, and Applied Materials, up 1-1/4 to 29-1/4.
The long bond lost 10/32 to yield 6.83 percent on technical factors and Fed Governor Lawrence Lindsey's comments that curbing inflation may mean a temporary rise in future interest rates.
There was also some fear in the bond market that Friday's producer prices and retail sales reports for September could be "mildly unfriendly" for bonds.

"The bond market was ahead of itself and with a 6.75 percent yield assumed everything would go perfectly. There was no margin of error for stocks or bonds. If the figures prove reassuring, it's already in the market. Again, the market is in a no-win situation," said Michael Metz, Oppenheimer and Co's chief investment strategist.
As for stocks, Cardillo said, "People are leery here. We're waiting to see the parade of earnings come out. Are we waiting for a 10 percent correction? Now? Absolutely not."
He said Wall Street did not really believe the Yeltsin rumor, which the State Department said was "totally unfounded."
A State Department spokesman said the United States had checked the rumors with the Russian government through the U.S. ambassador in Moscow.
"There was no flight to safety," said Cardillo, who noted bonds and the dollar did not get a lift from the rumor.

Among individual stocks, communications innovator PairGain Technologies tumbled 6-1/2 to 74-1/4 on profit-taking, analysts said, after the company reported a jump in third-quarter earnings on sharply higher revenues. CS First Boston downgraded the stock.
Tellabs soared six to 79 after posting stronger results.
U.S. Surgical added 2-1/8 to 45-3/4 after introducing the first set of instruments for minimally invasive coronary bypass graft surgery and the chairman's forecast that 1997 sales would accelerate.
Lason Holdings, which offers integrated outsourcing services for records and document management, rose 2-3/4 to 19-3/4 in its Wall Street debut.

One market highlight was news that Morgan Stanley's chief U.S. equity strategist Byron Wien boosted stocks by five percent to 85 percent and cut cash by five percent to 15 percent in his model U.S. equity portfolio.

Morgan Stanley said the move reflected Wien's view that interest rates may go down due to some signs of temporary weakness in the economy and as a result there may be a 10 percent upside to the stock market in the next six months.
Wien had been forecasting a 1,000 point fall in the Dow industrials in the near term.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 2.17 to 1237.98.
The S&P 500 index fell 3.90 to 696.74.
(Figures official as of 1645 EDT/2045 GMT)
-- Wall Street desk 212 859 1721
